name: Neurodegeneration with Brain Iron Accumulation Type 2

criteria.description: Progressive dystonia and parkinsonism with onset in childhood or adolescence
MRI evidence of iron accumulation in the globus pallidus and substantia nigra
Biallelic pathogenic variants in the PLA2G6 gene
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy on neuroimaging
Exclusion of other causes of neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive dystonia/parkinsonism, MRI evidence of brain iron accumulation, and biallelic pathogenic PLA2G6 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is essential for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Brain iron accumulation visible on MRI
pathognomonic.notes: Hypointense signals on T2-weighted images in globus pallidus and substantia nigra
searchTerms: iron buildup in brain seen on MRI
brain iron deposits visible on scan
excess iron accumulation in brain tissue
mental health symptoms like anxiety and depression

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of neurodegeneration
imaging: MRI showing hypointense signals in globus pallidus and substantia nigra on T2-weighted images
Cerebral and cerebellar atrophy in advanced stages
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in PLA2G6 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
other: Neurophysiological studies may show peripheral neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: PKAN typically shows 'eye of the tiger' sign on MRI
Earlier onset dystonia with pigmentary retinopathy
Multisystem involvement including muscle weakness and lactic acidosis
Variable MRI findings without prominent brain iron accumulation

redFlags: Rapidly progressive dystonia with early parkinsonism
MRI evidence of brain iron accumulation in basal ganglia
Family history suggestive of autosomal recessive inheritance
references: Gregory A, Hayflick SJ. Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation. Handb Clin Neurol. 2018;147:293-305.
Morgan NV, et al. PLA2G6 mutations cause infantile neuroaxonal dystrophy. Am J Hum Genet. 2006;79(4):942-949.
Le Ber I, et al. PLA2G6-associated neurodegeneration: a new neurodegenerative disorder with brain iron accumulation. Neurology. 2008;70(19 Pt 2):1826-1830.
